regulatory_and_risk_profile: Explainability required for claim and pricing denials
Legacy policy-administration systems with limited APIs
paper_process_blockers: Actuarial review of any pricing model change
Regulatory filing clocks for rate or form changes
Compliance review of claims-handling changes before automation touches live files
Change requests to the core policy system
dominant_friction: Combined-ratio pressure makes every change look expensive, and every denial must be explainable to a regulator.
value_frame: Anchor on loss-ratio compression, claims cycle-time reduction, human-in-the-loop audit trails, and elastic peak-volume pricing.

buying_committee.primary_fear: Automated pricing drifts, and we find out only after a bad loss year.
Automation denies a valid claim and triggers a regulatory complaint.
We cannot explain a denial to a regulator in plain language.
A model change goes live without actuarial sign-off.

signature_objections: Our combined ratio is already under pressure. Why would we add a new variable cost line?
When a claim gets denied by your model, what does the adjuster tell the policyholder?
Catastrophe season triples our claim volume for six weeks. Does your pricing spike with it?

metrics.speaker: Chief Underwriting Officer
metrics.partial: We track loss ratio every month, but the AI piece is not in the scorecard yet.
metrics.verbatim: I need claims cycle time down from twenty-one days to seven, and loss ratio must improve by at least two points, or this does not get funded.

economic_buyer.speaker: Head of Claims
economic_buyer.partial: Claims owns the workflow, but underwriting controls the budget for shared tools.
economic_buyer.verbatim: I own the claims operations budget and can approve up to the pilot cap alone. The production tier goes to the CFO.

decision_criteria.speaker: General Counsel
decision_criteria.partial: Explainability and fair-claims compliance matter a lot to my team.
decision_criteria.verbatim: Every denial needs a plain-language reason an adjuster can read to a policyholder, and we will not go live without that.

decision_process.speaker: General Counsel
decision_process.partial: Anything touching pricing goes through actuarial review, and the timing depends on the filing.
decision_process.verbatim: Pricing changes go to actuarial review, then the rate filing on a sixty-day clock. Claims automation goes to compliance first.

paper_process.speaker: General Counsel
paper_process.partial: Claims-handling changes need a compliance review before anything runs on live files.
paper_process.verbatim: No automation touches a live claim file until compliance signs off on the claims-handling change, and that review takes about six weeks.

identify_pain.speaker: Head of Claims
identify_pain.partial: Adjusters are buried in simple claims while complex ones wait.
identify_pain.verbatim: We have a backlog of 4,000 open claims, and severity leakage on simple auto claims costs us real money every quarter.

champion.speaker: Chief Underwriting Officer
champion.partial: I like where this is going, and my team has been asking for something like it.
champion.verbatim: I will take this to the leadership team myself, and I need the audit trail design in writing before I do.

competition.speaker: Head of Claims
competition.partial: Our core policy vendor has a claims module we have been meaning to look at.
competition.verbatim: Our core policy vendor is quoting its own claims automation for free if we renew, so you must show a better loss-ratio case than that.
